audits.title: 139 “Never Event, Never Again” - a Closed Loop Audit on the Documentation of Nasogastric Tube Position Following X-Ray Confirmation
audits.standard: Documentation of nasogastric tube position after X-ray confirmation using the NGT documentation sticker (Never Event prevention)
audits.setting: ENT ward, Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast

cycle1.result: Sticker used 42.1%; patient identity verified 39.5%; most recent X-ray confirmed 44.7%; time and date verified 34.2%; NGT position documented 63.1%; feeding instructions 65.8%; confirming staff recorded 60.5%.

audits.intervention: Teaching doctors to use the sticker supplied with each NGT pack, ward posters, and reminding nurses to check documentation before feeding.

cycle2.result: Sticker used 85%; identity verified 100%; most recent X-ray 100%; time and date 85%; position documented 75%; feeding instructions 75%; confirming staff 75%.

audits.other_findings: 58 chest X-rays were reviewed in total across both cycles.
audits.citation: Iosif G, Tan C, McCadden L. 139 “Never Event, Never Again” - a Closed Loop Audit on the Documentation of Nasogastric Tube Position Following X-Ray Confirmation. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.084.

audits.title: EP274 - A clinical audit on nasogastric tube placement documentation and adherence with NICE guidelines in general surgical patients across a district general hospital
audits.standard: NICE guidance on confirming NG tube position by aspirate pH testing or X-ray if indeterminate
audits.setting: General surgery department, district general hospital, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Correctly documented NG tube position confirmation 60%; feeding tubes 4/4 correct; drainage tubes 45.5% correct; insertion length documented 33.3%; X-ray requested and documented in all inconclusive pH cases.

audits.citation: Vickers C, Mukhtar I, Dhavala P, Arbis A. EP274 - A clinical audit on nasogastric tube placement documentation and adherence with NICE guidelines in general surgical patients across a district general hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.465.

audits.title: Avoiding never events: improving nasogastric intubation practice and standards.
audits.standard: National Patient Safety Agency guidance on nasogastric tube placement (never event)

cycle1.result: Seven junior doctor check-image interpretation errors in the mis-sited tube cohort.

audits.intervention: Recommendations on documentation, intubation, interpretation training (e-learning package) and radiology; new protocols for radiologists and radiographers.

cycle2.result: Interpretation errors reduced from seven to one; documentation improved by 22%.

audits.other_findings: Service still not perfect; radiology should lead on reducing misinterpretation risk.
audits.citation: Law RL, Pullyblank AM, Eveleigh M, Slack N. Avoiding never events: improving nasogastric intubation practice and standards. Clin Radiol. 2013;68(3):239-244. doi:10.1016/j.crad.2012.08.001. PMID: 22959258.

audits.title: Complications of nasogastric tube insertion in critical care: A retrospective analysis of radiographs performed for determination of tube position.
audits.setting: Critical care, Royal Liverpool University Hospital

cycle1.result: 10% of radiographs showed incorrect NGT position; all airway (11/512) and proximal oesophageal (5/512) tubes removed; only 51% (18/35) of suboptimal tubes were advanced

audits.other_findings: In 46% (16/35) of suboptimal cases radiology reports did not comment on safety or advise advancement.
audits.citation: Watkin D, Farrell C, McGee M, Welters I. Complications of nasogastric tube insertion in critical care: A retrospective analysis of radiographs performed for determination of tube position. Radiography (Lond). 2025;31(3):102941. doi:10.1016/j.radi.2025.102941. PMID: 40199191.

audits.title: Placement and Confirmation of Nasogastric Tubes: An Audit of Clinical Practices at a Pakistani Tertiary Care Hospital.
audits.standard: Evidence-based NG tube placement protocols (confirmation by chest X-ray or whoosh test)

cycle1.result: Cycle 1: whoosh test 50 (77%); chest X-ray 39 (60%); aspiration pneumonia 54% (n=27), down from 88.46% (46) pre-implementation (60 patients).

audits.intervention: Implementation of evidence-based protocols with repeated training workshops on placement, confirmation and follow-up care.

cycle2.result: Cycle 3: chest X-ray 96.03% (97); whoosh test 101 (100%); aspiration pneumonia 5%.

audits.other_findings: Cycle 2 (80 patients): chest X-ray 76.25%, whoosh test 90%, aspiration pneumonia 20.83%. pH testing was performed in 0% in all cycles.
audits.citation: Iqbal A, Gohar A, Hassan SH, Waheed S, Ullah AS, Ali A, et al.. Placement and Confirmation of Nasogastric Tubes: An Audit of Clinical Practices at a Pakistani Tertiary Care Hospital. Cureus. 2025;17(5):e84408. doi:10.7759/cureus.84408. PMID: 40535392.
